newsitem.title: USA: Syria refused to hold Saudi blast suspect - report.
newsitem.headline: Syria refused to hold Saudi blast suspect - report.

text.p: Months before the June bombing of a U.S. military housing complex in Saudi Arabia, Syria refused to help Saudi authorities capture a Saudi dissident who has been identified as the mastermind of the terrorist blast, the Washington Post reported on Saturday.

Quoting Arab sources and court documents, the newspaper said the Saudi government was hunting the dissident, Ahmed Ibrahim Mughassil, because it suspected him of involvement in the earlier bombing of a U.S. military facility in Riyadh and believed he was planning further attacks.

Mughassil was with the Hizbollah militia in Lebanon, a country dominated by Syria, but Damascus declined to help apprehend him because it was unwilling to risk an armed clash with the radical Islamic group, the Post said.

As a result, Mughassil, a leader of the Saudi branch of Hizbollah, remained at large. He is now listed by Canadian security officials as one of the "known conspirators" in the June 25, 1996, truck bombing that killed 19 American servicemen at the Khobar Towers housing complex in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia.

Mughassil was named in court papers filed in Canada in connection with the arrest there of another Khobar Towers suspect Hani Abed Rahim Sayegh. The Post said Mughassil was now believed to be in Iran.
